references.text: God's early promise to Abraham that his descendants would be as numerous as the dust of the earth – one of the first promises of countless offspring, expanded in Gen 22:17.
God leads Abraham out under the starry sky and promises that his descendants will be as numerous as the stars – the most direct parallel to the image of the stars in Gen 22:17.
Rebekah's family blesses her with words saying that her offspring will take possession of their enemies' gates, a direct echo of the promise in Gen 22:17.
God repeats the promise of countless descendants to Isaac, using the image of the stars in the sky, just as it was given to Abraham.
God renews the promise to Jacob about numerous offspring spreading in all directions, continuing the patriarchal promise.
Jacob reminds God of the promise to make his descendants as numerous as the sand of the sea, a direct connection to Abraham's blessing.
Moses notes that the Lord has made Israel as numerous as the stars in the sky, fulfilling the promise given to Abraham.
God promises that David's descendants and the Levites will be as numerous as the host of heaven and the sand of the sea, a parallel to the promise concerning Abraham's offspring.
The Letter to the Hebrews refers to God's oath to Abraham after the offering of Isaac, quoting the promise of abundant blessing and countless descendants.
Hebrews mentions that Abraham received descendants as numerous as the stars and the sand by the seashore, a direct reference to the patriarchal promise.
The original covenant formulation (12:2) serving as the foundation for the more specific promises in 22:17.
Transfer of the covenant to Jacob: the promise of fruitfulness and land given to Abraham's offspring is repeated here.
Parallel in victory over enemies: 'take possession of gates' (22:17) and 'devour the enemy' (9:15).
Confirmation of the covenant: the promise that Abraham will become a nation and kings.
Prophetic confirmation of Abraham's promise: 'your offspring as the sand' as a sign of God's faithfulness.
Fulfillment of Abraham's promise: to take possession of the land and become more numerous than the fathers.
Prophetic restoration of Abraham's promise: to make the people numerous and settled in the land.
Complementary promise: The universal blessing (12:3) as the foundation for Abraham's offspring (22:17).
Fulfillment of Abraham's promise in David's time: destruction of enemies and a great name.
The covenant formulation of Abraham's promise: to become numerous and take possession of the land through obedience.
Repetition of David's fulfillment of Abraham's promise to destroy enemies.
